result:
The proposed answer of 1 is wrong, because the solution misstates what MDS means.

A code is MDS when every set of k columns of the generator matrix is linearly independent, equivalently when every k×k minor is nonzero. The solution instead claims that any n−k+1 columns must be dependent, and that is a different condition. Having more than k columns in F_q^k forces dependence among them, so this condition holds trivially and says nothing about MDS. The argument therefore proves nothing.

A heuristic for the true limit: each of the C(n,k) minors of a random k×n matrix is singular with probability about 1/q. The expected number of singular minors is then about C(n,k)/q → λ. In this regime the singular minors behave approximately like independent rare events, so their count is asymptotically Poisson(λ). The probability that none are singular is therefore about e^{-λ}, which is strictly less than 1 for λ>0. I did not prove the Poisson approximation here, but the answer 1 is ruled out regardless, since the expected number of failing minors is a positive constant.

VERDICT: REJECT
